newsitem.title: UK: UK appeal court reserves judgment on Nadir aide.
newsitem.headline: UK appeal court reserves judgment on Nadir aide.

text.p: The London Court of Appeal on Friday reserved judgment on the money-laundering conviction of Elizabeth Forsyth, a former aide of Polly Peck head Asil Nadir, at the end of a two-day hearing.

"We desire to reserve our judgement in this matter...we will give our decision as soon as we can," Lord Justice Beldam told the court. Forsyth walked free on bail on Thursday after the judges allowed her appeal against her five-year sentence.
UK appeal court reserves judgment on Nadir aide
The judges said they were unable to give an immediate result as the appeal had raised complex issues.

Forsyth, 60, spent 10 months in prison after being found guilty last year on two counts of dishonestly handling a total of 400,000 pounds ($640,000), which the prosecution said had been stolen from Polly Peck that collapsed in 1990 under massive debts, by Nadir.
Nadir still faces fraud and theft charges in Britain but he fled to his native northern Cyprus in 1993, jumping bail of 3.5 million pounds.

On Thursday, Beldam described the original sentence handed out to Forsyth as "disproportionate". The judges said the sentence could not stand and this led to an application for bail and Forsyth's release. ($1=.6237 Pound)
